1. Melt butter over medium heat.
2. Add onions, carrots, celery and bay leaves and cook until the veggies begin to get tender, about 5 minutes.
3. Add garlic, plus a pinch of salt and pepper, stir, and cook about 30 seconds more.

6. Increase the heat slightly to medium-high. [...] 9 ounces chicken cooked and shredded - I used leftover store-bought rotisserie chicken
 1/4 cup butter diced into 1 tbsp pieces
 1 medium yellow onion diced
 1 cup carrots diced
 1 stalk celery diced
 2 leaves bay
 4 cloves medium garlic minced
 1/3 cup all-purpose flour
 6 cups chicken broth (I used 6 cups water + 2 Tablespoons Better than Bullion chicken base)
 1 1/2 cups of 1% milk
 3 medium russet potatoes peeled and diced to 1/2-inch thickness [...] Chicken corn chowder is a creamy, delicious and filling soup that is like a little hug in a bowl. Chicken, corn, potatoes, carrots, celery, onion, garlic in a creamy broth, topped with bacon, green onions and cheese.

And who couldn’t use a hug in a bowl right about now?!🙋🏼‍♀️

# Chicken Corn Chowder Recipe

By: Author Jenny Bullistron

29 Comments

Jump to Recipe  Print Recipe

This chicken corn chowder recipe is creamy and hearty comfort food. The recipe is easy to follow and full of veggies – corn, potatoes, carrots, and celery! Also, you can save time by using a store-bought rotisserie chicken.

We still have to deal with cool nights as the weather gets warmer and the days get longer. [...] In a large soup pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
 When the oil is hot, sauté the onions for 5 minutes. Then add the celery and carrots, stirring frequently and sautéing for 5 minutes.
 Add the chicken broth, corn, chicken and potatoes. Increase heat to medium-high and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
 Add the half and half and paprika. Cook for an additional 10 minutes or until the chowder returns to eating temperature.
 Season to taste with salt and pepper. [...] Don’t skimp on the ingredients.Part of what makes this chicken corn chowder so great are the vegetables and the potatoes, so don’t cut back on their quantity. In fact, maybe even add more!
 Lighter version. If you want to lighten the calorie count, substitute 1% or skim milk. It will be less creamy, but the flavor is still fantastic.
 How much chowder? This is going to make A LOT of chowder. If you aren’t ready to eat chowder for a few days and aren’t cooking for a crowd, halve the recipe.

output.title: Creamy Chicken Potato Soup (with added veggies) - The Natural Nurturer
output.content:
This creamy chicken potato soup recipe makes 6 hearty servings in 1-pot, with each portion (about 1.5 cups each) rocking peas, carrots, bits of cooked chicken thigh and (of course) chunks of perfectly tender Yukon gold potatoes. The potatoes add a lovely heartiness to the soup and, after the veggies + chicken simmer to to perfection in the broth, you scoop out some of those lovely buttery potatoes and blend them with some Greek yogurt. This simple step makes the soup even creamier while keeping [...] 1 Tablespoon olive oil
 1 Tablespoon butter, or additional oil
 1 medium onion, chopped
 4 cloves garlic, minced
 1½ teaspoons salt, divided
 ½ teaspoon ground black pepper, divided
 ½ teaspoon dried rosemary
 ½ teaspoon dried oregano
 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into ½-inch dice
 1 pound Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cut into ½-inch dice
 4 cups low sodium chicken broth
 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken thighs
 ½ cup plain whole milk Greek yogurt , or sour cream [...] Add oil and butter to a large soup pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, ½ tsp of salt, and ¼ tsp of pepper. Sauté for 2 minutes to soften the onions.
 Stir in the rosemary, oregano, carrots, potatoes, and chicken broth. Nestle the chicken thighs in the soup, making sure they are fully covered by the broth.
 Bring the soup up to a low simmer and cook until the chicken thighs are cooked through, 10 to 12 minutes.
